forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Waverley reports £2.9m General Fund and £3.0m housing account underspends for 2025/26
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council ended 2025/26 with a £2.9m underspend on its General Fund, the account that pays for services funded by council tax and business rates. Its housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for council housing paid for by rents, underspent by £3.0m. The figures are in the annual report of the council's external auditor, which went to the Audit & Risk Committee on 16 November 2026.

The General Fund underspend compares with £1.7m in 2024/25, and the housing account's with £1.02m. The General Fund result includes £2.4m of staffing savings and £1.7m of treasury income.

The auditor's report says: "While the General Fund and HRA outturn positions were favourable, these were influenced by non-recurring factors rather than the delivery of recurring savings." It says both results were driven by non-recurring factors.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 4 - Waverley BC Auditor's Annual Report (AAR) 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: Waverley opened 2026/27 with a £7.3m general fund deficit, forecast to narrow to £4.5m by year-end
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council began the 2026/27 financial year with its main day-to-day account (the general fund) £7.3m in deficit, and forecasts it will end the year £4.5m in deficit, according to budget papers for its Executive committee on 6 October. The council puts the £2.8m improvement down to £1.1m of budget movements and £1.7m from commitments, money already set aside for specific purposes.

The papers show a similar pattern in the money set aside against business rates, the tax on commercial property. The reserve for timing differences on government grants and for spreading the cost of a deficit started the year £3.75m in deficit. Budget movements of £2.67m are forecast to bring that to £1.08m in deficit. A separate reserve covering risks to the council's medium-term financial plan, its multi-year forecast of spending against income, is forecast at minus £665k, after £197k of budget movements and £280k of commitments.

Two income lines are forecast below budget. Planning land charges, the fees for property searches, are expected to bring in £345,565 against a budget of £406,070, a shortfall of £60,505 or 14.9%. Commercial Waverley Training Services is forecast at £368,965 against £406,635, a shortfall of £37,670 or 8.5%.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB Capital Programme Report Q2 2026 QC LL
findings.headline: The planned works team is using an interim planned works surveyor appointed via agency for 3 months to cover capacity challenges.
findings.detail: The interim appointment covers identified capacity challenges in the planned works team. The paper also records that procurement delays are generally caused by local government reorganisation (s24 LGR).
findings.matters: Interim cover and reorganisation-linked procurement delays are pressures other councils and their finance teams may be managing at the same time.
findings.quote: Delay on procurement generally caused by s24 LGR.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB Capital Programme Report Q2 2026 QC LL
findings.headline: A £500k budget risk for the new kitchen and bathroom budget has been moved to existing kitchen and bathroom and window and door contracts.
findings.detail: The paper says the sum has been moved into existing contracts and that the urgent roofing contract value is being increased. Executive approval for contract increases and virements is listed as a pending governance item.
findings.matters: Reallocating a large sum between contracts before executive approval shows how a council manages scope changes inside a fixed capital envelope.
findings.quote: Budget risk of £500k for new Kitchen & Bathroom (K&B) budget moved to existing K&B and window & door contracts

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB Capital Programme Report Q2 2026 QC LL
findings.headline: The paths, parking and curtilage budget of £50k is at risk of overspend because of required health and safety works
findings.detail: The overspend risk arises from H&S works that are needed. The council plans to request a virement once the value is confirmed, and a potential virement request for this area is listed among the governance items.
findings.matters: A budget heading moving into overspend that is funded by virement shows how a council handles a cost pressure within its existing capital envelope.
findings.quote: This is at risk of overspend

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB Capital Programme Report Q2 2026 QC LL
findings.headline: The structural budget of £200k is likely to underspend, while insurers have yet to respond to the council's claims.
findings.detail: Three structural projects (two houses and one block) are at investigation or monitoring stages. The council has chased the insurers regularly without a response on its claims.
findings.matters: An expected underspend that depends on insurer decisions carries timing and recovery risk, which other councils holding similar budgets would also need to manage.
findings.quote: therefore this budget is likely to underspend.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB Capital Programme Report Q2 2026 QC LL
findings.headline: The roofing programme's start was delayed by a challenge to the tender process from one of the tendering contractors.
findings.detail: The paper records that the roofing contract, awarded to Cardo South, was delayed by a challenge. The contractor was at mobilisation stage in the reporting period, with replacement of roofs due to start at the end of October.
findings.matters: Procurement challenges that delay a major contract are a recurring source of slippage in capital programmes, and the timing affects how much of the year's budget can be spent.
findings.figures: Roofing start: end of October 2026 (per paper)
findings.quote: Delay on Roofing contract – caused by challenges to tender process by one of the tendering contractors

daily_post.headline: The Audit & Risk Committee agreed in November 2024 to appoint up to two independent members, and none had been appointed by the end of 2025/26
daily_post.lead: An audit committee without its agreed independent members is a governance point a finance director at another council would check in their own arrangements.
